title: avoid apologies alarm ambiguity in dialog titles
name: Avoid apologies alarm ambiguity in dialog titles — MUI
rule: Avoid apologies, alarm, or ambiguity in dialog titles — not "Sorry for the interruption", "Warning!", or "Are you sure?". Dual-cite Atlassian error-title (3–4 words, not "what to do") — MUI is the banned-title list on the dialog itself.
pass_when: Dialog title (when present) is not an apology, "Warning!", or "Are you sure?".
overview: Dialog titles avoid apologies, alarm, and vague “Are you sure?” wording.
apply_when: Writing a title on a confirmation or alert dialog.
not_when: Not for body copy, button labels, or title-less ordinary alerts.
agent_hint: Ban Sorry, Warning!, and Are you sure? from dialog titles; name the decision.
description: When a dialog has a title, avoid apologies, alarm, or ambiguity—not “Sorry for the interruption”, “Warning!”, or “Are you sure?”. The title should name the decision so people can scan the dialog and buttons with confidence. Apologetic or alarming titles add noise without clarifying the choice. Fail when those banned titles appear on the dialog. Apply when writing titles on confirmation or alert dialogs.
do_not_claim: `actions.confirm.specific_consequences` as a delete of this banned-list row. Overlap with Actions 40: `actions.confirm.specific_consequences`.
